Bathroom Deep Cleaning: Remove Hard Water Stains and Mold

Hard water stains and mold are the two most frustrating bathroom problems in Jalandhar. Here is how to tackle both — and when to call a professional.

What Causes Hard Water Stains?

Jalandhar's water has high mineral content. When water dries on glass, tiles, and fixtures, it leaves behind calcium and magnesium deposits. Over time, these build into a white, crusty film that regular cleaners cannot remove.

How to Remove Hard Water Stains

For light stains: white vinegar and water (1:1) sprayed on the surface, let sit for 10 minutes, then scrub with a microfiber cloth. For heavy stains: use a commercial descaling product or citric acid solution. For glass shower doors, a razor blade scraper works wonders — but be careful not to scratch.

How to Prevent Mold

Mold thrives in damp, poorly ventilated bathrooms. Run the exhaust fan during and after showers. Wipe down wet surfaces daily. Use a squeegee on glass doors. Seal grout lines annually. If mold keeps returning despite these steps, you may have a moisture issue behind the tiles.

When to Call a Professional

How Often Should You Deep Clean Your Home? A Room-by-Room Guide

Most people know they should deep clean their home "regularly" — but what does that actually mean? Here is a practical, room-by-room guide based on how your home actually lives.

The General Rule: Every 3–6 Months

For most homes, a full deep clean every 3–6 months is sufficient — assuming you keep up with weekly cleaning in between. Homes with pets, children, or allergy sufferers should lean toward the 3-month end of the spectrum.

Kitchen: Every 2–3 Months

Grease and food residue accumulate faster here than anywhere else. Deep clean the oven, refrigerator, range hood, and behind appliances every 2–3 months. Wipe cabinet fronts and clean the dishwasher filter at the same time.

Bathrooms: Every 2–3 Months

Bathrooms need deep attention to grout, caulking, shower glass, and exhaust fans. Mold and hard water stains develop gradually and become harder to remove the longer you wait.

Bedrooms: Every 3–4 Months

Dust, dead skin cells, and allergens accumulate in mattresses, under furniture, and in carpet fibers. Deep clean ceiling fans, baseboards, under the bed, and closet interiors.

Living Areas: Every 3–4 Months

Focus on upholstered furniture, carpets, air vents, and window tracks. Move furniture to vacuum underneath. If you have pets, increase to every 2–3 months.

Sofa Cleaning 101: Dry Clean vs Steam Clean vs Shampoo

Your sofa accumulates more dirt, dust, and bacteria than you think. But which cleaning method is right for your fabric? Here is everything you need to know.

Dry Cleaning (Solvent-Based)

Dry cleaning uses a solvent-based foam that is applied, agitated, and vacuumed. It dries fast (1–2 hours) and is ideal for delicate fabrics like velvet, silk, and antique upholstery. CleanNest's dry clean service starts at ₹199 per seat.

Steam Cleaning (Hot Water Extraction)

Steam cleaning injects hot water and cleaning solution into the fabric, then extracts everything with a powerful vacuum. It removes deep-set dirt, allergens, and bacteria. Best for cotton, linen, and synthetic blends. Drying time is 3–5 hours. CleanNest's premium + steam service is ₹349 per seat.

Shampooing (Bonnet Cleaning)

Shampooing uses a rotating brush to work foam into the fabric surface. It is effective for surface-level dirt but does not reach deep into the cushion. Best for high-traffic commercial upholstery. Less common for home sofas.

Which Should You Choose?

For most modern home sofas, premium clean (₹279/seat) is the sweet spot — it removes deep dirt without the long drying time of steam. If you have allergies, pets, or heavy stains, go with premium + steam (₹349/seat). Delicate fabrics: dry clean only (₹199/seat).
